techniques.target: render 0x9E54 + copy 0x9E6B at 28 MHz in original-time windows; in-between views on scratch pages 38-41; K by a run-time calibration render
main loop 0x9E34: 7-21 frame updates, no frame wait
ORIGINAL per update: window = K x the render's 28 MHz lines, signed debt
JNext pace log vs the plain build, 178 updates
route 2a: update 0x9E34 as N = 1 / 2 / 4 sub-steps (adaptive) at 28 MHz; driver at 0x9E2F / 0xFC4C, physics hooks with 8-bit fractions, 12 gates, render guards
route 2a: REAL TIME, 3,110 lines an original update; view copies on an absolute schedule (line clock NR 0x1E / 0x1F), debt capped at 3 frames
route 2a: bank 12: Sinclair's ROM 1 + the steps trampolines at 0x3870

pacing.coverage: First 3,000-6,000 frames of hard_drivin.rzx (229 updates profiled); the whole RZX for the verify; JNext 4,000 frames for pace; hardware not measured.
pacing.result: No frame wait; updates 7-21 frames (median 13); the render 87 % and the copy 6 % of an update; the lap clock counts updates, so each update's original time must be kept.

dependencies.coverage: Render window 0x9EA9..0x9E57 over 2,500 frames for consumers; the whole RZX for the differential verify; the 0xA402 time-out path not reached.
dependencies.result: 23 addresses the render leaves are read later by logic; the real render runs last on the genuine pages so they stay as the original leaves them; in-between views run on scratch pages only. R not preserved (no consumer found).

feasibility.decision: Smoother 3D view (user, 2026-11-22): render and copy at 28 MHz held to the original's time per update; in-between views in the freed time; K measured at run time.
feasibility.next_experiment: Hardware: pace within 1 % of the plain build over 100 updates, and no tearing in the view.
